text:
maria: ran a quick nsys pass on a dedicated pod to investigate the kernel selection flapping we saw at p99 yesterday. attaching rough notes here, want opinions on safe sampling windows before we try in-canary :thinking_face:

jason: can you paste the nsys command you used?

maria: sure — used a light capture around hot requests:```bash
nsys profile --output=out_profile --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,cudamem --duration=10s --force --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi
# then nvtx ranges around tokenize->kv lookup->attention
```
It's not full GPU memcpy timeline but gives kernel order and stack. Observed: a small fraction of requests hit a slower kernel path (matmul fallback) when batch size jittered between 4 and 6.

anika: interesting — what's the overhead of that nsys snippet? even 10s could perturb scheduling on small pods.

maria: measured ~18-22% end-to-end latency increase during the capture window on that instance (very bursty). GPU utilization also looked spikier. Not safe to run wide.

samir: 18-22% matches expectations for full tracing. We should avoid full captures on production. Options: very sparse sampling, synthetic load on a mirrored node, or micro-probes that only NVTX keypoints and kernel timestamps.

elena: for KV cache behavior we only need to know timing when cache miss hits the memory path. Could we set a tracer that only fires on misses (e.g., set an env flag to emit nvtx for cold-path + 1s window)?

maria: tried that — added a conditional NVTX push around "kv.lookup if miss" and limited to 1 in 1000 requests. Overhead ~0.9% from our load test. Data quality: we captured clean kernel timelines for cold-paths, but p99 behavior is noisy because the miss distribution is extremely bursty.

jason: that sounds promising. Two follow-ups: 1) how do we ensure the tracer doesn't interact with batching logic (i.e., we don't change batch boundaries)? 2) how to quantify confidence in sampled estimates?

maria: 1) guarding NVTX alone didn't change batch boundaries in our tests because we only push a marker, no locks. But when we enabled a full nsys capture (even short), the profiler pause collapsed a few micro-batching windows causing a fallback kernel to appear more often. So rule: do not do full-agent captures on production batching nodes.

maria: 2) confidence — we need an estimate of sampling variance. For cold-path events (rare), use importance sampling: bias sample prob up for requests that report "cache_miss=true" in request metadata; then weight the observations accordingly. With 1/100 miss rate and 1/10 sampling of misses, effective sample rate for misses ~0.1. variance still high but tractable.

anika: can we get an offline emulator for kernel-selection decisions? feed the real batch-size/time-of-arrival traces and run the kernel-selection logic standalone. That would let us identify thresholds causing fallback without touching prod.

samir: we already have a local playback harness (perf-play) but it uses synthetic kernels. We should extend it to replay real KV miss timing and variable sequence lengths. Might catch a rare combo that triggers the slow kernel.

elena: for guardrails I propose: 1) sampled NVTX probes only (no full-system capture) by default; 2) cap sampling to <=1% of requests per node and <=5% overall; 3) if we detect sampling-induced p99 delta >5% on a node, auto-disable sampling for 30m and alert; 4) separate probe for KV-miss cold-paths with higher sampling probability but limited to X events/hour.

ops-bot: deploy-check: sampling config change requires a canary rollout to 5% nodes, monitoring p50/p90/p99 delta, and a kill-switch in the console.

jason: sounds reasonable. We should add a lightweight perf counter option (perf event sampling) as a complement — ~2-3% overhead, lower fidelity on CUDA kernels but good for CPU-side batching heuristics and scheduling hotspots.

maria: noted. My plan:
- implement NVTX-only probe that is conditionally emitted: ``if env.SAFE_PROBE == "1" and random() < sampling_rate`` and a special header for cache_miss-based upweighting
- extend perf-play to replay arrival patterns and KV miss signals
- add guardrail automation (node-level feedback disable)

samir: add a short RFC doc with: expected overhead numbers, sampling math for confidence intervals, and fail-open semantics. I'll review.

anika: also add a small dashboard: sampled_rate, observed p50/p90/p99 delta during sampling windows, count of sampled cold-path traces, and average kernel-switch time.

maria: will draft RFC tonight. quick note on numbers we observed: full nsys ~18–22% e2e overhead for 10s window; NVTX-only sampling at 0.1% per-request ~0.9% overhead measured; perf-event CPU sampling ~2.5% on small instances. Use those as ballpark in RFC.

elena: agreed. Also add a mitigation: if we see a new kernel variant appear in samples, route matching traffic to a safe fallback model (pin older quantized kernels) while we triage.

jason: nice. One last ask — can we mark which metrics are safe to expose in the public tenant console vs. internal-only (NVTX payloads may contain model identifiers and must stay internal)?

maria: yes — NVTX trace payloads will be internal-only. Aggregates (counts, timings, deltas) can be surfaced with redaction.

samir: +1. I'll comment inline on the RFC.

maria: thanks all — I'll open the RFC and a 5% canary PR with the NVTX-only probe and perf-play changes.

elena: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: ticket created: INF-4921 "pulse-check: NVTX sampling probe + guardrails" assigned to maria, reviewers samir, anika, jason

maria: added links in the RFC to the sample traces and perf-play patch when ready.

jason: awesome, ping me when canary is up and I'll monitor kernel switch events.

maria: will do.
